title: Foundations
intro: The mathematical language of quantum mechanics and its first three postulates: states are unit vectors, measurements are probabilistic and disturbing, and observables are Hermitian operators.

blocks.text: Quantum mechanics is linear algebra over the complex numbers, plus one rule that turns vectors into probabilities. This topic sets up both. Nothing here depends on a particular physical system; the qubit, which is the main example, gets its own topic next.

items: Linear Algebra for Quantum Mechanics (#/quantum/foundations/linear-algebra): complex vectors, inner products, Hermitian and unitary matrices, eigen-decomposition, matrix exponentials and Kronecker products.
States and Dirac Notation (#/quantum/foundations/states-and-dirac-notation): kets, bras, superposition, bases, and why global phase does not matter while relative phase does.
Measurement and the Born Rule (#/quantum/foundations/measurement): probabilities from amplitudes, collapse, measuring in other bases, and the statistics of repeated shots.
Observables and Uncertainty (#/quantum/foundations/observables-and-uncertainty): expectation values, variance, commutators and the uncertainty relation.

blocks.text: If you only read one page before the QRC shelf, read Measurement and the Born Rule. The single fact that a feature like $\langle Z\rangle$ must be estimated from many destructive shots shapes half of what QRC hardware can and cannot do.
